family.note: Clustered by prologue/n-gram similarity only. draw_item_price.c is a straight-line goto-based single-price display; the real owner is a 15-entry loop over a u16 flag array, each entry tested against a 0x200 'active' bit, masked to a 9-bit item id, looked up via Func_08077018, then switched on the returned struct's byte-2 'type' field (1..4) to pick a draw style (8/56/40/24) for Func_08015080. Only the shared UI-draw-call idiom (Value_00000182 message-base convention) carried over; the control shape is unrelated to the template.

notes: Read the real assembly directly: outer loop counts sl from 14 down to 0 (15 iterations) over a caller-supplied `const u16 *flags` array; per entry, tests `entry & 0x200`, then `item_id = entry & 0x1ff`, calls Func_08077018(item_id) to get an item-info pointer, and switches on info[2] with case order 2, (>2: 3,4), 1 -- a decision-tree shape consistent with a plain `switch(type){case 1: case 2: case 3: case 4:}` lowering, which is what my candidate wrote.

First candidate (switch-based, pointer-walking loop over flags, matching the case bodies and Func_08015080(item_id+(s32)&Value_00000182, window, 8, style) call form) diverges immediately in the prologue: my code precomputes the 0x200 mask via `movs r2,#128; lsls r2,r2,#2` (arithmetic synthesis) where the reference loads it from the literal pool (`ldr r3,[pc,#36]`). The reference also loads the flag halfword with a plain `ldrh` while my compiled candidate produced an `ldrsh` with an indexed (register-offset) addressing mode instead of the reference's simple post-increment-style `[r7,#0]` -- suggesting my `for(i=14;i>=0;i--){ value=*entry; entry++; }` shape got strength-reduced differently than the reference's structure by this compiler.

This is a genuine source-shape gap, not yet reduced to a single respelling: the algorithm, field offsets, mask/id values, and per-type call arguments all read correctly off the assembly, but the exact loop induction-variable form (pointer-only vs index+pointer) and the small-constant materialization choice (pool load vs shift synthesis for 0x200) need at least one more structural rewrite (e.g. drop the separate `i` counter and loop purely off the pointer test, or model the counter as the primary induction variable with array-indexed access) before another measurement is worthwhile.
